correctness.rationale: The quantifier-rank-two Ehrenfeucht–Fraisse game for a finite nonempty strict poset sees exactly which of the 3-bit pointed profiles (exists lower, exists upper, exists incomparable) occur; each profile is definable with at most two nested quantifiers and Duplicator matches any selected pointed profile. Incomparability-graph connected components are linearly ordered by the poset, so its ordinal-sum decomposition constrains signatures to 2 singleton/antichain cases, 4 nontrivial connected cases and 16 multi-component displays, with exactly two duplicated sets: 20 distinct rank-two theories. All 20 lower-bound witnesses are explicit downset tuples. The exceptional mask 232 requires two nontrivial endpoint components, a middle interior point, and an additional element for type 111, hence >=6; its six-element witness attains it. Independently generated naturally labelled posets by adjoining an ideal-supported maximal vertex, with per-size counts 1,2,7,40,357,4824 for n=1..6 and verified exact all-20 minimum masks, with mask 232 unique at size 6. Exhaustion through n=6 supports the table; global exclusion follows from ordinal-sum proof, not that census.
